Use the model above to calculate the value of $2÷\frac{5}{8}.$
question.worked_solution:
To calculate $2÷\frac{5}{8}$, we first need to divide each of the $2$ wholes into $8$ equal parts.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/79dcc7dffe163a88185b222516bcf278959e8d2844d133ad8515dcd302b5937b.png)

 

Next, we break this into groups of $5$:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/59a293c88f1ffa513065465f0fe602bf9ba547b7af7d91a3e4ad3d757343f9d9.png)

 

Note the following: 

- We got $\boxed{\text{3}}$ full groups.

- There is $1$ piece left over out of a possible group of $5.$ So the fractional part of our answer is 

$$
\frac{1}{5}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
2÷\frac{5}{8}=\boxed{\text{3}}\,\frac{1}{5}.
$$
